gaps.sentence: I ___ in this city since 2015, and I still love it.
gaps.hint: since 2015 plus still means it continues
gaps.explanation: 'Since 2015' with 'still' marks a situation continuing to the present, so the present perfect is used: have lived.

gaps.sentence: I usually cycle to work, but this week I ___ the bus because my bike is being repaired.
gaps.hint: this week contrasts with the usual habit
gaps.explanation: 'But this week' signals a temporary arrangement around now, so the present continuous is correct: am taking.

gaps.sentence: When she was a student, she ___ spend her summers hitchhiking around Europe.
gaps.hint: a repeated past action with would
gaps.explanation: 'Would' describes repeated past actions in narrative: would spend.

gaps.sentence: I ___ you were coming today — nobody told me!
gaps.hint: state verb forbids the past continuous
gaps.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb, so its past form is the past simple: didn't know.

gaps.sentence: By the age of thirty, she ___ her own company.
gaps.hint: by the age of means completed before
gaps.explanation: An achievement completed before a past reference point takes the past perfect: had started.

gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.

gaps.sentence: By next April, we ___ here for ten years.
gaps.hint: duration leading up to a future point
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a future point takes the future perfect continuous: will have been living.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.
